title: Stroke segmentation: agents draw SVG rings and part scribbles on multiview pictures, lifted onto the scan like stroke_sculpt
user-messages: another thing I think I want a ticket for since I archived the automatatic sgementation is a similar path that the sculpting tool uses to allow agents to draw svgs on a sculpt we should do something similar here for segmentation instead of trying to get the agents to click individual points, look online a t the literature for that
description:
Let segmentation agents draw SVG strokes on multiview pictures of a scan, the way stroke-sculpt agents already do, and lift those strokes onto the surface as rings and part labels. This replaces clicking ring anchors one point at a time in the ring scene.

## Why

The automatic segmentation (crease maxima seeding rings, CRAW-102) is archived. In the CRAW-95..100 crawfish runs, the segmenters spent most of their time clicking anchors through `ixdar-cli control`, then screenshotting to check them. `reports/tool-review-2026-11-06.md` in ai-workspace shows this: 1,181 of the reads were screenshot images, plus 341 hover, click and key calls. The sculpt path works the other way round. The agent gets a multiview picture, draws weighted SVG paths on it, and `StrokeSketch` / `StrokeLift` cast CPU rays through the camera stored in the SVG to land each path on the mesh (`stroke_sculpt` node, the stroke-sculpt skill). Drawing a whole groove in one path is what a picture-reading agent is good at. Placing points one by one is not.

## Literature (sketch-based mesh segmentation)

A comparative study of interactive mesh cutting (Fan et al., cited by NICOGRAPH 2014) sorts the interfaces by what the stroke means:

1. **Along the boundary.** The stroke traces the cut.
   - Funkhouser et al. 2004, "Modeling by Example" (intelligent scissoring): a 2D line starts a cut, which is closed into a loop and relaxed like a snake toward concave contours (the minima rule).
   - Ji et al. 2006, "Easy Mesh Cutting" (CGF 25(3)): freehand sketches with region growing under a feature-sensitive metric, plus boundary optimisation.
   - This maps onto `spline_ring`: one SVG path gives a ring's visible side. CRAW-61 is the same idea for a human dragging on screen.
2. **Foreground and background scribbles.** The stroke paints inside a part.
   - Fan, Liu, Liu 2011, "Paint Mesh Cutting" (CGF 30(2)): one stroke on the part, then a local graph cut over Gaussian mixtures of the shape diameter function.
   - This maps onto `add_label`: a scribble carries the part name.
3. **Across the boundary.**
   - Zheng and Tai 2010, "Mesh Decomposition with Cross-Boundary Brushes" (Eurographics): a short stroke across the seam, with the cut found where the stroke meets the concavity.
4. **Lifting 2D masks from many views.**
   - Tang et al. 2024, "Segment Any Mesh" (arXiv 2408.13679): render the mesh from icosahedral views, segment each picture, then lift through rendered face ids into a match graph across views.
   - This is our multiview capture plus a face-id pass. The agent's drawing plays the part of SAM's masks.
   - The licence of github.com/gtangg12/samesh has not been checked; read nothing from it until it has.

Also relevant: Dot Scissor (Zheng et al. 2011, concavity-aware fields, single click), already discussed under CRAW-102.

## Shape of the change (to be settled in the design step)

- The agent captures multiview pictures with the camera embedded, as stroke-sculpt does.
- It draws SVG paths, each tagged with a kind (ring boundary, or part scribble with a label) and a view.
- A route previews the lift, as `/mesh/stroke-lift` does.
- A DSL node, or a translation to existing `spline_ring` / `add_label` statements, turns the lifted strokes into the segmentation, so the result stays editable in the ring tool.
- The far side of a boundary stroke closes the way rings already do, or by a second stroke in another view.

## Constraint

No tuned thresholds or scales (Ixdar CLAUDE.md). Snapping a lifted stroke to the seam must not hide a picked radius, and neither may graph-cut weights. The papers above all carry such weights. Each one the design keeps goes in the ticket for the user to decide.

## Design (draft 2026-11-08, for the user to decide)

What exists to build on:
- `multiview --svg` writes the cells with their cameras in the SVG root.
- `StrokeSketch.lift` casts each polyline's pixels onto the mesh through the camera of its cell.
- `spline_ring` takes surface points as `points="x,y,z; ..."`. In `mode=crease` it already runs once round the part along the cheapest crease path through those anchors in order.
- `add_label` takes surface points too. Each point picks the ring region that holds it, so a label needs just one point inside its part.

That means a segmentation can come out as the DSL we already write, with no new node.

**D1. Output: plain statements (recommended).** A new route and CLI command, `stroke-segment --svg pass.svg --dsl seg.dsl`, lifts the SVG and writes or replaces:
- one `spline_ring(..., mode=crease, points=<lifted>)` for each `<polyline data-kind="ring" data-label="...">`;
- one `add_label(label=..., points=<lifted>)` for each `<polyline|circle data-kind="label" data-label="...">`.

The ring tool and judges see ordinary rings they can edit. The alternative is a `stroke_segment` node that holds the SVG the way `stroke_sculpt` does. It keeps the drawing as the source, but the ring tool can't edit it.

**D2. Where a ring stroke's anchors land.** An agent's line is a few pixels off the groove.
- (a) Take the lifted points as drawn. Crease mode still follows the groove *between* anchors, but each anchor is held exactly where it was drawn.
- (b) **Recommended.** Move each lifted point across the stroke, uphill on crease strength, until the next step is no stronger. That is a comparison, with no radius. The anchors land on the groove's crest.
- (c) Hand the stroke's endpoints only to crease mode. This throws the drawing away.

**D3. Anchor count.** The lift keeps points every `StrokeSketch.spacing` (0.03 world units by default). That is a tuned number. Proposal: take the mesh's own mean edge length as the spacing for segmentation strokes, so the data sets it. Each anchor is a pass-through point, so dense anchors just follow the drawing.

**D4. The hidden side.** Crease mode closes the ring once round the part from front anchors alone. A second stroke drawn in another cell with the same `data-label` adds anchors. Points from every cell are ordered by angle round the fitted ring plane, which needs only comparisons. To check: does a front-only stroke close where the groove really runs on IMG_4113?

**D5. CRAW-61.** It becomes the human front end to the same lift: drag on screen, get the same `spline_ring`. Close CRAW-61 in favour of this ticket, or keep it as a follow-up.

Numbers this inherits from the sculpt lift, for the user:
- `StrokeSketch.GRAZING_COSINE = 0.25`: points on surface seen nearly edge-on are dropped.
- The `spline_ring` supporting-anchor tolerance, which already exists.

Neither one is new. Option (b) of D2 adds none.

## Decisions (user, 2026-11-08)
- D1 output as plain spline_ring / add_label statements; D3 spacing from the mesh's mean edge length.
- D2: build both, snapped and as drawn, and test both ways; the user worries snapping will confuse agents.
- D5: CRAW-61 closed in favour of this ticket.

## Plan (agreed 2026-11-08): strokes as DSL nodes, no route

The `/ring/stroke-segment` route built so far breaks the rule that automation routes do no geometry: it lifts the SVG onto the surface itself (`RingStrokes.lift`). The work moves into nodes. The route goes, and so does the lifting in `RingStrokes`:

```
strokes = svg_to_curves(svg="dsl/crawfish/IMG_4113_strokes.svg")
lifted = project_curves(geometry=surface.geometry, curves=strokes.geometry)
ring_00 = spline_ring(..., curve=lifted.geometry, curve_index=0, mode="crease")
```

- **`project_curves` (new node):** casts one ray per pixel along each curve through its cell's camera, and keeps the curve on one continuous piece of the mesh. Neighbouring hits must lie on faces that share a vertex; where they don't, even at half-pixel steps, the line has slipped through a gap (the flap seam slit on IMG_4113 landed a point on the far flap's inner face). The curve keeps its longest unbroken run, and the dropped points are carried as an attribute. The output is `CurveGeometry` lying on the surface, with the SVG's `data-kind` and `data-label`.
- **`spline_ring` curve input:** its anchors and plane come from a lifted curve in place of `points` and `normal`. The plane comes from the camera rays through the curve's end pixels, not from the hit chord.
- **Labels:** `add_label` reads points from a lifted label curve the same way.
- **In the engine:** the ring scene draws the lifted curves (the trail view, today's `strokes` look) and the rings built from them, straight from the DSL. Opening the DSL shows everything; no CLI command and no launch property is needed.
- **Crease mode fix kept:** spans that share a vertex are searched again with the other spans blocked (`AuthoredSplineRing.trace`).
- **Still open:** the spline fitted through a sharp corner at an off-crease anchor can cross itself; see `CreaseRingTest.aCreaseRingThroughSeveralAnchorsNeverRunsOutAndBackAlongAStem` at 16 rings off.
definition-of-done:
1. A design section on this ticket picks the stroke meanings and the output form, listing every number the lift or snap uses for the user to decide.
2. An agent can capture multiview pictures of a scan, draw SVG strokes, preview their lift through a route, and save them as DSL that loads in the ring scene.
3. The mesh-segment skill describes the stroke path for segmenters.
4. A launch.json entry and screenshots under tmp/ show IMG_4113 segmented from strokes.
testing-plan:
1. Unit test: an SVG path drawn round a tube's waist in a known camera lifts to a closed ring on that waist.
2. Unit test: a labelled scribble on one end of a two-part shape labels that part only.
3. Run the stroke path on IMG_4113 and compare region count and boundaries with the hand-made segmentation.

changes-made: RingStrokes lifts data-kind=ring/label polylines through the SVG's cell cameras (optional crease-crest climb); /ring/stroke-segment (ixdar-cli stroke-segment --svg [--snap] [--preview]) writes crease spline_rings and add_labels into the ring scene's DSL, traces each ring first and reports a failing stroke on its own row, writes minted ring ids back into the SVG, reloads. RingStrokesTest covers both modes on a notched tube.

Per the user (one way to do things), stroke-segment now goes through the ring tool: ClosedRingTool.draftThrough (also the preview click's path) drafts each ring stroke in crease mode, RingTool.confirmDraft confirms it as Enter does, RegionLayer.namePart (shared with the label command) names parts, RingScene.saveRingsPressed saves as Ctrl+S. The DSL-writing path and --preview are gone. IMG_4113 abdomen example: 2 strokes refused by the tool's self-crossing check, 2 rings confirmed (length 0.22, 0.27) but the tool's own region rebuild reports both split nothing, so the surface stays one region.

Why stroke rings split nothing on IMG_4113 (2026-11-08): neighbouring abdominal side flaps touch, so the surface stays connected round any single abdomen ring. CRAW-95's hand ring_02 alone also splits nothing; with its side-flap rings ring_06 and ring_07 it splits (8 regions). The stroke ring at the same groove plus those two side rings splits the tail off the same way (tmp/craw-105-stroke-sides.png). So stroke segmentation must also draw the side-flap seams, from a side view.

2026-11-12 split: the worktree held four other pieces of work with no ticket. They moved to their own worktrees: the ring anchor fit to craw-106 (CRAW-106), the settle, curve fit and ring patch network experiments to craw-107 (CRAW-107, to be closed without landing), the grow tool to craw-108 (CRAW-108), the connection tool's leak finder and cut to craw-109 (CRAW-109), the toolbar to ui-21 (UI-21). This worktree is down from 91 changed files to 42, all stroke segmentation, and compiles. Review: ai-workspace reports/craw-105-uncommitted-review-2026-11-12.md. Snapshot of the worktree before the split: ai-workspace tmp/craw-105-split/.

2026-11-14: the stroke arrows (SurfaceArrows.atLineEnds, drawn by RingScene under the strokes look) no longer build cos/sin rings by hand. A unit arrow is now made by evaluating the primitive nodes through MapNodeContext: a cylinder node (shaft) and a cone node (head), each 12 segments, moved by transform_geometry and joined by join_geometry. Each line then scales it with transform_geometry, aims it with align_rotation_to_vector (taking +Y onto each end's heading) and places it at both ends with instance_on_points, and the lines are joined with join_geometry. The primitive nodes are unchanged. The proportions are unchanged (length 0.25 of the line's chord, shaft radius 0.04, head radius 0.12, head 0.4 of the length). Before and after, same camera: tmp/craw-105-arrows-before.png and tmp/craw-105-arrows-after.png (0.04% of pixels differ). CRAW-105 re-creates no sphere geometry: stroke dots are the existing SurfaceDots. Also synced onto master (UI-21 toolbar, UI-20 glyphs, CRAW-111); the conflicts were resolved keeping both sides (ControlHint Keys API; Shift+T confirms an open draft first).
